I don't like websites that give additional permissions to people who comment. I understand that it encourages participation, and participation is certainly key for a small community. Do you prefer quantity over quality? Or do you disagree with my ideas entirely?

This idea has been posted many times over at /v/ideasforvoat where I recently argued for the opposite:

https://voat.co/v/ideasforvoat/comments/119366

I agree that the voting limits promote participation, but like the old saying goes, “Wise men speak because they have something to say; fools because they have to say something.” You don't want to encourage participation because the only contributions worth reading are from people that actually have something useful to say.

But quality is also harmed if the fool is given power over what should and should not be read. The ability to downvote and upvote are as I said in that thread achieved in such a short span of time compared to the time you will be active, that any wise man would see that it is worth his effort to contribute. To me the lurker often isn't the person most able to appreciate and thus stimulate quality. The subverses with the most points and with the least posts (or most lurkers per points) such as /v/funny don't prove to me the competence of lurkers.

I don't think this can be resolved unless we get some data on lurker/non-lurker voting habits.

In any case, we're in the minority of people that prefer in-depth comments instead of over-used memes. Since quality is subjective, who are we (as active users) to determine for everyone (including lurkers) what is a quality post? Lurkers are in the majority on the internet. If the goal is to make most people happy, we should give everyone unlimited voting rights.

I just wanted to challenge myself, so I am switching from Ryu/Sagat/Guile to Guy. Are there tips from going from a fireball based character to a non fireball character?

Could I play Guy in a defensive style? Or does he need to be played in your face? Thanks!
[Need help] Switching from Ryu/Sagat/Guile to Guy. Tips on switching from fireball to non fireball!

Ah! I'm a Guy main, I'll sum this up as best as I can.

Guy's defensive options are weird. He's a counter-hit monster if you can get inside their head. His elbow drop is mainly useful for baiting actions. Just like his overhead cancel. If you press F+MP, guy does his 2 hit overhead. You can cancel it into any special within a few frames. His MK Tatsu is also fireball invincible below his waist. His defense lies in guiding the opponents offense, and if they play along, predicting and scoring massive damage on counter-hits.

You can play him defensively but it's best to utilize his defensive options once and use them to slip in and start applying pressure. His Hozanto goes under projectiles and high attacks. His flip is almost impossible to react to, if you're in the corner and sense an opening, a HP Bushin flip will almost always gain you a ton of real estate.

His crouching LK is an amazing whiff punish tool, and it's got impressive range. And, since you can cancel it, it can be an amazing tool for punishing. Whiff punishing everything with a LK xx Runslide/runstop depending will stop any Shotos from their crouching MK xx Fireball.

Standing medium kick is an awesome poke. No combo potential, but it's got deceptive range. At focus range, you can use his MP like a grappling hook if you cancel into runstop and bait if they block. Or you can follow with target combo if they Focus counter, or if they FABD you can cancel into runslide. Or poke with medium punch and cancel into light bushin flip, once or twice.

He's incredibly versatile but his weaknesses are deep. He doesn't have many ways to counter pressure. His main reversal EX Tatsu isn't really his main reversal. It's a good "DP" style wakeup but it's risky. a better option is EX run, it's armor cancellable, and it has 2 hits of armor, and stop adds one more hit of armor. The EX run slide goes under fireballs, the EX run neckflip is low strike and fireball invincible.

What do you think of the Assassins Creed series?

I played 1 and 2, but couldn't really get into them. I was all for being an assassin, but the modern day story bored me.

I got Black Flag when the XB1 was released and I've probably put 500 hours into it, it's easily in my top 10 games. It's incredibly fun, the story is great and the modern day part doesn't interfere with game play too much. I would absolutely love a sequel to this game, even though it's never going to happen. Being a pirate was awesome.

I purchased Unity and didn't really enjoy it, it is a beautiful looking game, but the story was short and the ending was really cliche.

Here's hoping the next game is fun,
I was into the modern day story during the first one, the end . I thought it sucked in 2, but the Ezio story picked up the slack big time.

I loved Black Flag as well. I think the weakest part of the game was the overarching plot. The piracy storyline and mechanics were top notch, but they kept inserting the Templars into it and that felt like a distraction from the fun parts of the game.
Agreed, take away the templars and the stupid office simulator and it'd be an amazing stand alone pirate game.

AC1 was above average for me. I had a good bit of fun running around assassinating things. Once you finished the main story it got a bit repetitive, but that's just the nature of most video games. AC2 was more of AC1, but with a graphic and gameplay update so that's an automatic win. Everything seemed to slowly go downhill after Brotherhood. I stopped checking in on the series in general halfway through AC3. I guess churning games out yearly has an effect on their quality.

I remember seeing the E3 trailer for AC1 back in high school, and I remember getting really excited for it. I've played every game except for Rogue, and have played many of them multiple times.

I'd have to say that AC1, 2, and 3 are my favorites, and probably in that order as well. I didn't actually care much for Black Flag as an Assassins Creed game. I think it's a great pirate game that features some Assassins, but it didn't feel like it belonged in the series.

I'm a bit concerned about where the series is going. I think Ubi has to make a clear decision about the modern day story; either commit to it, and provide a quality modern day story, or scrap it and forget about it. Unity's modern day story was a half-assed mess that never should have happened.

With that said there are some encouraging directions the series is moving in. I think the murder mysteries in Unity were awesome, and I hope they keep going with them in Syndicate. I'm also excited that they scrapped the multiplayer to focus on a quality single player story; though I'm disappointed they gave up on the coop missions.

Overall, I'm still a fan of AC, though not nearly as die hard as I once was. I haven't bought an AC on launch since 3, and unless E3 blows me away, I likely won't get Syndicate on launch either, but I will still play it.
